title: Localized Photon Absorption in a Single-Crystalline Material
summary: The absorption of light is one of the most fundamental processes in condensed-matter physics and optics. Here we investigate under which conditions laser light is absorbed by a crystalline material as an electromagnetic wave with delocalized properties or rather as photons that cause discrete, localized, nanometer-sized consequences. We excite the first-order phase transition of vanadium dioxide with laser pulses of sufficient frequency to overcome the band gap but with insufficient pulse energy to overcome the latent heat.
